statement.p: Find f if \nabla f=2xy\,\vec i+(x^{2}+5y^{4})\,\vec j

static.solution: \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 2xy\quad\hbox{and}\quad \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = x^{2}+5y^{4}. Now think of y as a constant in the equation for \partial f/\partial x and integrate, giving f(x,y) = x^2y + C(y). Since the constant of integration may depend on y, it is written C(y). Differentiating this expression for f(x,y) with respect to y and using the fact that \partial f/\partial y = x^{2}+5y^{4}, we get \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} = x^2 + C'(y) = x^{2}+5y^{4}. Therefore C'(y) = 5 y^{4}\quad\hbox{so}\quad C(y)=1 y^{5} + K. for some constant K. Thus, f(x,y) = 1x^{2}y+1y^{5}+K.
